question.text: For a Cat III AIF that accepts subscriptions and redemptions using daily NAV, the Valuation Day is BEST defined as:

answer.text: Any day the manager feels appropriate
Only the last day of the financial year
The day pre-determined by the AIF and communicated in offer documents, as the day by reference to which the NAV is determined

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'The Valuation Day is pre-determined by a Category III AIF, and communicated to the investors in its offer documents, as the day by reference to which the NAV of the Category III AIF is determined.' The same chapter notes the allowed frequency can be daily (e.g., listed-only portfolios), monthly, or another pre-defined cadence. The Trap: Manager discretion without disclosure is not permitted; financial-year-end-only conflicts with periodic NAV reporting; month-end is a permitted but not the only option. Note: Two attributes define the Valuation Day - it must be pre-determined by the AIF and disclosed in the offer documents.
